strings.device.auto_filter.analog_a_gentle_satur: Analog — a gentle saturation after the filter, like an analog circuit
strings.device.auto_filter.cutoff_the_base_the_m: Cutoff — the base the modulation moves from; the dashed mark is where it is now. Double-click resets, ⌥-click types a value.
strings.device.auto_filter.drag_sideways_for_the: Drag sideways for the cutoff, up and down for the resonance. The teal band is how far the envelope and LFO can move the cutoff; the dashed curve is where they have it now.
strings.device.auto_filter.hold_keep_the_envelop: Hold — keep the envelope at its peak for the HOLD time before it releases (∞ freezes it)
strings.device.auto_filter.resonance_the_peak_at: Resonance — the peak at the cutoff; the dashed mark is where it is now. Double-click resets, ⌥-click types a value.
strings.device.auto_filter.retrig_restart_the_lf: Retrig — restart the LFO on each input onset (−24 dBFS) and when play starts
strings.device.auto_filter.sidechain_key_the_env: Sidechain key — the envelope follows another track instead of this one. Switch on to pick the source and the key gain; right-click to change it.
strings.device.auto_filter.stereo_phase_the_righ: Stereo phase — the right channel's LFO runs ahead of the left (90° when switched on; right-click steps 45° … 180°)
strings.device.auto_filter.the_inputs_envelope_t: The input's envelope (teal) and the cutoff it drives (neutral ink), the base cutoff dashed. Drag up or down for the amount.
strings.device.auto_filter.the_lfos_movement_ove: The LFO's movement over the window — raw shape dashed, what the filter follows (after Smooth) in neutral ink, the right channel in rose when stereo is on. Drag up or down for the amount, sideways for the start phase.
strings.device.auto_gain.auto_rides_the_gain_to: Auto rides the gain to the target over Window; Manual holds the fader where you put it (Match sets it to the distance to the target)
strings.device.auto_gain.ceiling_6_0_dbtp_drag: Ceiling, −6 … 0 dBTP — drag up / down (Shift for fine steps), ⌥-click to type, double-click resets to −1.0
strings.device.auto_gain.input_loudness_on_the_c: Input loudness on the chosen scale (LUFS); the teal mark is the target
strings.device.auto_gain.input_silent_the_measur: Input silent: the measurement and the gain hold
strings.device.auto_gain.leveler_bypassed_the_ou: Leveler bypassed: the output equals the input
strings.device.auto_gain.match_set_the_manual_ga: Match — set the manual gain to the distance between the measured input and the target
strings.device.auto_gain.max_gain_the_most_the: Max gain — the most the correction may boost or cut, 0 … 24 dB
strings.device.auto_gain.output_loudness_on_the_: Output loudness on the chosen scale (LUFS); the teal mark is the target
strings.device.auto_gain.output_lu_from_the_targ: Output {0} LU from the target · Match sets {1} dB
strings.device.auto_gain.output_true_peak_dbtp_t: Output true peak (dBTP); the teal mark is the ceiling while True-peak safe is on
strings.device.auto_gain.reset_restart_the_measu: Reset — restart the measurement from the loudness now, so the ride catches up at once
strings.device.auto_gain.response_slow_glides_ov: Response — Slow glides over the whole Window with a 20 ms look-ahead; Fast over a quarter of it with 5 ms
strings.device.auto_gain.scale_what_the_correcti: Scale — what the correction reads: Momentary (400 ms, fast and nervous), Short-term (3 s) or Integrated (12 s with BS.1770 gating, the steadiest)
strings.device.auto_gain.target_loudness_36_0_lu: Target loudness, −36 … 0 LUFS. Click the value for the standards or to match another track's loudness (a reference); drag the dashed line in the graph for the same
strings.device.auto_gain.the_correction_applied_: The correction applied, ±Max Gain around 0 dB (trim not included)
strings.device.auto_gain.the_correction_around_0: The correction around 0 dB, ±Max Gain. In Manual drag it (Shift for fine steps); ⌥-click types, double-click resets to 0 dB. In Auto it shows the ride
strings.device.auto_gain.the_last_8_s_input: The last 8 s: input, output and the target with its ±1 LU band (momentary loudness). Drag up / down to move the target; ⌥-click types, double-click resets it
strings.device.auto_gain.trim_a_fixed_offset_aft: Trim — a fixed offset after the correction, −12 … +12 dB (the output then sits that far off the target)
strings.device.auto_gain.true_peak_safe_a_look: True-peak safe — a look-ahead limiter keeps the output under the ceiling (adds 5 / 20 ms of latency, compensated)
strings.device.auto_gain.waiting_for_signal_the_: Waiting for signal — the gain holds until the input has been measured
strings.device.auto_gain.what_the_leveler_is_doi: What the leveler is doing now
strings.device.auto_gain.window_how_long_the_rid: Window — how long the ride takes to reach the target, 0.4 … 10 s (Fast: a quarter of it)
strings.device.auto_pan.180_auto_pan_one_side: 180° — auto-pan: one side up while the other is down
strings.device.auto_pan.90_a_quarter_cycle_apart: 90° — a quarter cycle apart: the sound circles
strings.device.auto_pan.above_8_hz_the_movement: Above 8 Hz the movement reads as a flutter, not as panning
strings.device.auto_pan.amount_or_mix_at_zero: Amount or Mix at zero: nothing moves
strings.device.auto_pan.amount_the_depth_each_ch: Amount — the depth: each channel dips to 1 − Amount at the LFO's low point
strings.device.auto_pan.both_channels_gain_over_: Both channels' gain over two LFO cycles — L neutral, R teal, Phase later — with the floor the depth reaches. Drag up / down for Amount, left / right for Phase; ⌥-click types, double-click resets both.
strings.device.auto_pan.mix_the_moving_signal_ag: Mix — the moving signal against the dry one
strings.device.auto_pan.panner_bypassed_the_sign: Panner bypassed: the signal passes unchanged
strings.device.auto_pan.phase_0_l_and_r: Phase 0°: L and R move together, the level dips to
strings.device.auto_pan.phase_the_right_lfo_agai: Phase — the right LFO against the left: 0° tremolo, 90° a circling pan, 180° auto-pan
strings.device.auto_pan.rate_the_free_lfo_rate: Rate — the free LFO rate, 0.01 … 40 Hz
strings.device.auto_pan.rate_the_note_value_of: Rate — the note value of one LFO cycle, 4/1 … 1/32 with dotted (D) and triplet (T) values
strings.device.auto_pan.shape_sharpens_sine_tri_: Shape — sharpens Sine, Tri and Saw toward a square; on S&H it is Glide, the slide from one step to the next
strings.device.auto_pan.the_channels_output_peak: The channel's output peak, −60 … 0 dBFS, and the gain the LFO gives it now, dB
strings.device.auto_pan.the_lfo_shape_s_h: The LFO shape. S&H draws a random step every cycle; the right channel plays the same steps Phase later
strings.device.auto_pan.what_the_phase_makes_tre: What the phase makes: tremolo near 0°, auto-pan near 180°, an offset pan between
strings.device.auto_pan.where_the_sound_sits_now: Where the sound sits now between left and right, over the swing the LFO covers
strings.device.auto_shift.amount_how_far_the_voi: Amount — how far the voice is pulled to the note
Amount — how far the voice is pulled to the target note
strings.device.auto_shift.bend_the_widest_move_b: Bend — the widest move between notes that bends over Glide; wider leaps jump
strings.device.auto_shift.custom_edit_on_the_sca: Custom — edit on the Scale tab
strings.device.auto_shift.follow_copy_the_key_an: Follow — copy the key and scale of a Nota Scale MIDI effect
Follow — copy the key and scale of a Nota Scale MIDI effect (this track, the MIDI source, or the first one found)
strings.device.auto_shift.from_the_instrument_tr: From — the instrument track whose notes set the target (its MIDI clips and effects, even when muted)
strings.device.auto_shift.glide_how_long_the_tar: Glide — how long the target bends from one note to the next (Pitch bend from MIDI)
strings.device.auto_shift.how_long_each_note_was: How long each note was sung (the last ~16 bars) over the scale's notes — neutral in the scale, teal outside it. Click a column to add or remove its note
strings.device.auto_shift.human_keeps_vibrato_an: Human — keeps vibrato and slow drift around the corrected note (0 = flat)
strings.device.auto_shift.key_source_auto_follow: Key source — Auto follows the key you sing, Manual uses the key and scale you set, MIDI takes the target from another track's notes (MIDI tab)
strings.device.auto_shift.key_the_tonic_the_scal: Key — the tonic; the scale's notes are counted from it
strings.device.auto_shift.latch_holds_the_target: latch holds the target between notes
strings.device.auto_shift.latch_keep_the_last_ta: Latch — keep the last target between notes (off = no correction while no note is held)
strings.device.auto_shift.learn_listen_to_what_i: Learn — listen to what is sung, then click again to set the key and scale that fit it best
strings.device.auto_shift.note_the_voice_goes_to: Note — the voice goes to the last held note; Scale — the held notes form the scale
strings.device.auto_shift.oct_lock_the_notes_own: Oct lock — the note's own octave (off = whichever octave of it is nearest the voice)
strings.device.auto_shift.pitch_bend_from_midi_m: Pitch bend from MIDI — moves between notes bend over Glide when they are within Bend; off = the target steps
strings.device.auto_shift.preserve_formants_the_: Preserve formants — the vowel colour stays put while the pitch moves (off = it moves with the pitch, like a tape speed-up)
strings.device.auto_shift.range_the_largest_corr: Range — the largest correction; a note further off than this is only pulled this far
strings.device.auto_shift.scale_chromatic_major_: Scale — Chromatic, Major, Minor, Pentatonic (major or minor — click again to swap) or Custom (the notes below)
strings.device.auto_shift.scale_the_notes_the_vo: Scale — the notes the voice is pulled to
strings.device.auto_shift.skip_sibilants_s_sh_t: Skip sibilants — s, sh, t and breath pass unshifted, so they don't turn metallic
strings.device.auto_shift.source_sets_the_detect: Source — sets the detection range for a voice type or an instrument
strings.device.auto_shift.speed_how_fast_the_ret: Speed — how fast the retune glides (2 ms = hard tune)
strings.device.auto_shift.speed_how_fast_the_voi: Speed — how fast the voice follows the target
strings.device.auto_shift.the_correction_now_up_: The correction now — up or down from the centre, full height = 2 semitones
strings.device.auto_shift.the_detected_pitch_low: The detected pitch, low to high across the detection range (Detect tab)
strings.device.auto_shift.the_detected_pitch_tea: The detected pitch (teal dots) and the corrected output (neutral ink) over the last two seconds, on the scale's note lanes; the target lane is lit
strings.device.auto_shift.the_key_that_fits_what: The key that fits what was sung (Krumhansl profiles over the last ~16 bars), and the runner-up. Learn sets it; Auto follows it
strings.device.auto_shift.the_source_tracks_note: The source track's notes (neutral blocks, accent while sounding) and the voice (teal) over the last two seconds — with Key Source MIDI the voice is pulled to the notes
strings.device.auto_shift.what_the_detector_hear: What the detector hears now and the correction applied — or, with Key Source MIDI, the note the voice is pulled to
strings.device.bass.mod_wheel_opens_the_lfo: Mod wheel — opens the LFO onto the cutoff
strings.device.bass.slide_into_a_note_played: Slide into a note played over a held one without a new attack
strings.device.beat_repeat.chance_how_likely_eac: Chance — how likely each interval fires a repeat
strings.device.beat_repeat.filter_off_or_a_low: Filter — Off, or a low-pass, band-pass or high-pass on the repeats
strings.device.beat_repeat.gate_how_long_the_bur: Gate — how long the burst lasts, in 16ths of the interval
strings.device.beat_repeat.grid_the_length_of_th: Grid — the length of the slice that repeats
strings.device.beat_repeat.interval_how_often_it: Interval — how often it rolls Chance
Interval — how often it rolls Chance: 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 note, or every 1, 2, 4 bars
strings.device.beat_repeat.latch_the_repeat_butt: Latch — the Repeat button stays on after a click instead of only while held
strings.device.beat_repeat.mode_mix_the_repeats_: Mode — Mix: the repeats play over the dry; Insert: they replace it while they play; Gate: only the burst sounds
strings.device.beat_repeat.narrow_with_repeats_e: Narrow with repeats — each repeat narrows the band and moves it with the pitch
strings.device.beat_repeat.offset_where_in_the_i: Offset — where in the interval it fires, in 16ths
strings.device.beat_repeat.pitch_decay_each_repe: Pitch decay — each repeat drops lower, up to 6 semitones a repeat
strings.device.beat_repeat.repeat_filter_the_rep: Repeat filter — the repeats go through the filter (Filter tab)
strings.device.beat_repeat.repeat_repeat_the_cur: Repeat — repeat the current slice now, for as long as it is held (with Latch: click on, click off)
strings.device.beat_repeat.reset_stop_the_repeat: Reset — stop the repeat and clear the timeline and the meters
strings.device.beat_repeat.the_last_intervals_so: The last interval's sound (teal) on the grid: the gate from the offset is shaded and the captured slice is brass. Drag the offset line or the gate's end sideways; ⌥-click to type, double-click resets.
strings.device.beat_repeat.the_repeat_filter_onl: The repeat filter — only the repeats go through it. Solid: the first repeat; teal dashed: a later one when the band narrows and follows the pitch. Drag the node for the frequency, a band edge for the width; ⌥-click to type, double-click resets.
strings.device.beat_repeat.the_repeats_level_aft: The repeats' level — after pitch, filter, decay and volume
strings.device.beat_repeat.triplet_the_grid_in_t: Triplet — the grid in triplets (a third shorter)
strings.device.beat_repeat.two_intervals_on_the_: Two intervals on the grid: each step is the input's level — dim when dry, full where the slice is captured, dimmer with every repeat as it decays. Ticks at the top mark where the interval fires.
strings.device.beat_repeat.variation_the_grid_fl: Variation — the grid floats up to this many steps (double / half) on each trigger
strings.device.beat_repeat.what_the_repeater_is_: What the repeater is doing now — waiting for the interval, capturing the slice, or repeating it — and where the transport is
strings.device.beat_repeat.width_the_band_in_oct: Width — the band in octaves (low- and high-pass: less is more resonant)
strings.device.card.changed_since_you_loaded_cho: Changed since you loaded {0} · choose a preset
strings.device.ceiling.auto_release_the_release_: Auto release — the release slows as the reduction deepens (up to 5× at 7 dB), so dense passages don't pump
strings.device.ceiling.ceiling_the_output_never_: Ceiling — the output never goes above it (in dBTP with True peak on)
strings.device.ceiling.character_clean_transpare: Character — Clean: transparent, the fastest attack; Punch: a slower attack lets the transient through to the clip; Glue: a slow release and a soft knee under the ceiling
strings.device.ceiling.delta_play_the_difference: Delta — play the difference between the input and the output: what the limiter takes away
strings.device.ceiling.gain_how_hard_the_signal: Gain — how hard the signal is driven into the ceiling
strings.device.ceiling.integrated_loudness_since: Integrated loudness since the last Reset, gated (BS.1770), against the Target
strings.device.ceiling.key_source_internal_limit: Key source — Internal limits on this track's own peaks; pick another track to duck this one when that one peaks
strings.device.ceiling.momentary_teal_short_term: Momentary (teal), short-term (neutral ink) and integrated (rose) loudness over the last 60 s around the target, ±1 LU shaded. Drag the target line; ⌥-click to type, double-click resets.
strings.device.ceiling.release_how_fast_the_gain: Release — how fast the gain comes back (the character scales it; Auto rel lets the signal decide)
strings.device.ceiling.reset_peaks_clear_the_pea: Reset peaks — clear the peak holds, the max reduction and the clip count
strings.device.ceiling.reset_start_the_integrate: Reset — start the integrated loudness, the range and the peaks again
strings.device.ceiling.target_the_loudness_the_m: Target — the loudness the meters compare against: −14 for streaming, −16 podcasts, −23 broadcast. It does not change the sound; drag the dashed line for any value
strings.device.ceiling.the_gain_reduction_over_t: The gain reduction over the last 4 s: teal where a transient got through to the clip, the dashed line is the mean
strings.device.ceiling.the_input_after_gain_with: The input after Gain, with the ceiling marked
strings.device.ceiling.the_last_4_s_the: The last 4 s: the input (teal), the part over the ceiling (red) and the output (neutral ink), with the reduction under it. Drag the ceiling line; ⌥-click to type, double-click resets.
strings.device.ceiling.true_peak_the_detector_re: True peak — the detector reads the inter-sample peak (4×), so the ceiling holds in dBTP after conversion
strings.device.ceiling.what_the_limiter_listens_: What the limiter listens to — or, with Delta on, that you are hearing only what it takes away
strings.device.chamber.algorithm_share_of_the_bl: Algorithm share of the blend (drags Blend)
strings.device.chamber.at_the_input_before_both: at the input, before both engines
strings.device.chamber.blend_convolution_slate_t: Blend — convolution (slate, top) ⇄ algorithm (neutral, bottom). Double-click: 50 / 50
strings.device.chamber.convolution_share_of_the_: Convolution share of the blend (drags Blend)
strings.device.chamber.drag_a_marker_to_set: Drag a marker to set that band's RT60 (mid = Decay; low / high follow it as ratios). The Damping knob sets the high crossover. · ⌥-click to type
strings.device.chamber.drag_the_trim_lines_to: Drag the trim lines to trim the IR (Start · Decay); ⌥-click to type, double-click resets. Drop an audio file here to load it.
strings.device.chamber.drop_an_impulse_response_: Drop an impulse response here (WAV / FLAC / MP3) or click Load…
strings.device.chamber.ducking_the_wet_dips_up: Ducking — the wet dips (up to 24 dB) while the input plays
strings.device.chamber.eco_ir_up_to_3: Eco: IR up to 3 s · Mid: 6 s · High: 10 s + cubic-interpolated algorithm modulation
strings.device.chamber.freeze_hold_the_algorithm: Freeze — hold the algorithm tail forever; the input is muted
strings.device.chamber.hold_in_keep_feeding_the: Hold in — keep feeding the input into the frozen tail (layering)
strings.device.chamber.impulse_response_built_in: Impulse response — built-in rooms, or your own file (drop it on the waveform)

strings.device.crush.dither_up_to_lsb_of: Dither — up to ±½ LSB of triangular noise before the levels: softens the steps into hiss
strings.device.crush.drive_12_24_db_into: Drive — −12 … +24 dB into the crusher: pushes the signal up the levels, into the Analog clip or into more folds
strings.device.crush.input_output_through_drive_: Input → output through Drive, the mode and the levels; the dot is where the signal peaks. Drag up / down for Drive; ⌥-click types, double-click resets.
strings.device.crush.jitter_the_hold_length_wand: Jitter — the hold length wanders up to ±50 %: an unsteady, broken clock
